entries.original_title: Altered prefrontal correlates of monetary anticipation and outcome in chronic pain
entries.original_authors: Martucci, Katherine; Borg, Nick; Macniven, Kim; Knutson, Brian; Mackey, Sean
entries.description: Martucci et al. (2018) reported that patients with fibromyalgia showed reduced medial prefrontal cortex responses during anticipation of monetary gains compared with healthy controls.
entries.citation_sentence: A previous study by Martucci et al. (2018) combining fMRI with the MID task found that brain responses to monetary reward are altered in patients with fibromyalgia.
entries.notes: The replication found the same-direction reduction as a non-significant trend, and the authors described the result as generally consistent but not fully replicated.

entries.original_title: Altered prefrontal correlates of monetary anticipation and outcome in chronic pain
entries.original_authors: Martucci, Katherine; Borg, Nick; Macniven, Kim; Knutson, Brian; Mackey, Sean
entries.description: Martucci et al. (2018) reported that patients with fibromyalgia showed enhanced medial prefrontal cortex responses to non-punishment monetary outcomes compared with healthy controls.
entries.citation_sentence: Compared to healthy controls, patients demonstrated reduced MPFC responses during the anticipation of reward gains, but enhanced MPFC responses in response to non-punishment outcomes.
entries.notes: The replication found the same-direction increase as a non-significant trend, which the authors treated as a generally similar but incomplete replication.

entries.original_title: Altered prefrontal correlates of monetary anticipation and outcome in chronic pain
entries.original_authors: Martucci, Katherine; Borg, Nick; Macniven, Kim; Knutson, Brian; Mackey, Sean
entries.description: Martucci et al. (2018) reported no difference between patients with fibromyalgia and healthy controls in nucleus accumbens response during anticipation of monetary gains.
entries.citation_sentence: NAcc responses during the anticipation of reward gains, however, did not significantly differ between patients vs. controls (Martucci et al., 2018).
entries.notes: This was an original null claim, and the replication also found no patient-control difference; the authors explicitly described the result as consistent.

entries.original_title: Altered prefrontal correlates of monetary anticipation and outcome in chronic pain
entries.original_authors: Martucci, Katherine; Borg, Nick; Macniven, Kim; Knutson, Brian; Mackey, Sean
entries.description: Martucci et al. (2018) reported that greater medial prefrontal cortex response to non-punishment outcomes was associated with greater mood disturbance.
entries.citation_sentence: These analyses suggested that across both studies, MPFC response to non-punishment outcome was positively correlated with individual differences in mood disturbance (i.e., greater MPFC response was related to higher mood disturbance as indicated by higher self-reported POMS scores).
entries.notes: The replication reproduced the positive association, although the within-group association was primarily driven by the fibromyalgia group.
